bounds.quantity: the marginal closure rate, worst junction
bounds.note: the cheap bound: a trio needs all three junctions to close on ONE lattice, and each junction's problem is independent of the others given the lattice. A zero here would kill the trio outright with no joint search at all

bounds.quantity: the independence yield of C-0059's own budget

bounds.quantity: the independence yield of one full lattice grid

findings.the verdict: A TORSION-FEASIBLE TRIO EXISTS. 21 of the 21 (crossbar, row) configurations carry one, the best leg chord 9.0° off the direction C-0048 wants and the best worst-of-three 21.0°, on a budget of 49857 lattices and 149789 junction solves against C-0059's 48 and 269
findings.why C-0059's negative carried no informa: its 24 solved lattices at two candidate azimuths per junction were worth 0.28 trios under the marginal census's own independence prediction, so a null result was the expected one. The deepened sweep returns 6 closing lattices at the same configuration
findings.the cheap bound: the three junctions close on 21 %, 20 % and 28 % of lattices marginally; the joint rate at the design point is 0.80 % against an independence prediction of 1.17 %, so the conjunction is HARDER than independence, not easier
findings.the verdict grid: 39 of the 44 reported trios still close when every junction is re-solved on C-0057's own 180-step / 6-refinement verdict grid, so the existence result does not rest on the search grid alone; the 5 that do not are the measure of how far a refined LOCAL zoom can move a closure, in both directions, and they are reported rather than dropped
findings.the row is one number: C-0059's design table composes a 9 bp base floor from the sheet with a 7 bp cap floor from the crossbar, but the row pitch IS the legs' separation and a leg has only one of those — CH-0075. Computed row by row at one pitch throughout, the best representable design is 10 bp row at BOTH ends: base 6.0°, cap 27.0° on the 17 bp crossbar at 12 steps, margin 2.45 on CanDo's rigidity and 1.84 on Fields et al.'s
findings.what this cannot establish: A torsion check is a NECESSARY condition and never a sufficient one, exactly as C-0029, C-0052 and C-0057 all said. A 'closes' verdict is an upper bound on buildability; nothing here is measured, no sequence is designed, and no assembly is demonstrated.
